title: Tune a ukulele's G string to pitch with a clip-on tuner
instruction: The ukulele's G string has gone flat. Tune it to G4 with the clip-on tuner. Then let go of the tuning button, pluck the G string once more to check it, and move both hands away from the ukulele.
context: Tuning is the first thing most players do on picking up a ukulele or guitar, and most people have watched it up close: one hand plucks the string again and again while the other turns that string's tuning button a little at a time until the clip-on tuner shows the right note, centred. The hard part is physical: the button is small, stiff and geared, and it must be stopped within 5 cents of pitch (about 23 degrees of the button either way), taking up the gear's free play whenever the turn reverses. The tuner reads only while the string rings, so between turns the other hand must pluck cleanly, pushing the string aside and letting it spring back untouched. The robot must also read the note as well as the needle (at the start F# reads centred and green) and pick the button that winds the G string, not the C string's beside it.
setup: Units mm. x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. Two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases at y = +305 and y = -305, start at their ready pose with grippers open; one overhead camera and one camera on each wrist. (1) Kala KA-15S soprano ukulele (satin mahogany, open-gear tuners with pearloid buttons, 346 mm scale, 535 mm long, lower bout 178 mm, body 60 mm deep), Aquila Super Nylgut strings in standard re-entrant tuning G4 C4 E4 A4. It stands on its side as it is held to play, soundboard vertical and facing the robot, neck parallel to the y axis, headstock to the robot's right: soundboard at x = 262 (back at x = 322), the neck's centre line 101 mm above the table, nut at y = -128, headstock tip at y = -249, tail at y = 286. So the G string is the top string, 9 mm in front of the soundboard. Its tuning button sticks straight up from the headstock's upper edge and is the one of the two buttons on that edge nearer the nut: a flat button 18 mm across, 12 mm long and 6 mm thick, centred at (282, -163, 143), its broad faces toward +y and -y. The C string's button is beside it, centred at (282, -200, 143); the E and A strings' buttons point down from the lower edge. The soundhole, 51 mm across, is centred at (262, 97, 101); the G string crosses it at x = 253, 118 mm above the table, and the body's upper edge is 166 mm above the table there. The cradle is two black closed-cell foam blocks (EVA or similar), 60 mm long, taped to the table: one under the body's lower edge at its widest point (y = 232, top 12 mm above the table), with 12 mm cheeks rising 15 mm up the soundboard and the back; one under the neck's lower edge at the 3rd fret (y = -73, top 82 mm above the table), with one cheek behind the neck (12 mm thick, rising 15 mm). One 25 mm hook-and-loop strap round the lower bout and its block, behind the bridge (y = 237 to 262), holds the body in the block. Nothing presses on the strings. The C, E and A strings are in tune (within 3 cents). The G string is 100 cents flat (F#4, within 5 cents). (2) Snark ST-2 clip-on chromatic tuner on the headstock tip, vibration mode, A4 = 440 Hz, its screen facing the robot and up, tilted 50 degrees from vertical, its middle at (224, -240, 114). While a plucked string sounds it shows the nearest note's name on a needle meter, green when in tune (in simulation it has lamps for F#, G and G# only, the needle swings 45 degrees left or right for 50 cents flat or sharp of that note, and green means within 3 cents). When no string sounds the screen is blank (in simulation every lamp is off and the needle rests at its left end). Nothing else is on the table. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: After the trial the judge plucks the G string once over the soundhole and reads a phone tuner app that shows cents (for example Pano Tuner, 20 cm from the soundhole). Within 5 cents of G4: 1.0 if the trial video shows the robot plucking the G string after its last turn of the G button and, in the video's last frame, both grippers' centre points are at least 50 mm from the ukulele and tuner; otherwise 0.75. Over 5 and up to 15 cents off: 0.75; up to 30: 0.5; up to 50: 0.25; over 50 either way: 0. Whatever the G string reads, the score is 0 if the C, E or A string reads more than 15 cents from its start (checked the same way, so turning the wrong button fails), the ukulele has left its blocks or the strap has come undone, the tuner has been knocked off, or a string has broken. In simulation the same bands are applied to each string's computed pitch at the last step; a pluck is as the fidelity note defines it; the G button counts as turned after a pluck once it is more than the gear's 4-degree free play from its angle at that pluck; the grippers' distance is measured to boxes around the ukulele's parts and the tuner; the ukulele and tuner are fixed and strings cannot break. In simulation the trial ends at the run limit or once 1.0 has held for 1 s; on the bench it runs to the run limit. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Retune C, E and A to pitch if they have drifted. Bring the G string to F#4 (100 cents flat, within 5 cents); approach it from below (loosen past it, then tighten up to it) so the gear's free play is taken up the same way every trial. Check the strap, the ukulele in its two blocks, and the tuner's position, angle and mode, and that it is switched on. Then pluck each string once and note its reading in cents: the scoring compares C, E and A with these. Nothing is consumed. New nylon strings keep stretching flat for about a week; use strings that hold pitch for a day.
fidelity: No sound is simulated. Pitch follows each button's angle: an estimated 0.22 cents per degree, with drag and about 4 degrees of gear free play. A pluck counts when the G string is pushed at least 2 mm across the strings over the soundhole and springs back untouched. The tuner is a stand-in (F#, G, G# and green lamps, a needle) showing the computed pitch for 3 s after a pluck, else unlit with its needle at the left end. No string stretch, drift or attack pitch rise; the ukulele is fixed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps; closed both grippers and never touched the ukulele); demo: 1.0 (675 steps; three plucks and one 455-degree turn of the G button with three regrips, ending at +0.05 cents, plucked again after letting go). Same fixed scene, rules and simulation scorer.
